PullRequest.Title: sessions: Sync Cloud Sandbox archives through Mission Control

## Summary

Cloud Sandbox archive operations currently update only the local session cache, so the owning Mission Control task remains unarchived and other clients continue listing it. This completes the cross-client work left open by [#337163](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337163), following the task ownership used for deletion in [#339042](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339042).

- Send archive/unarchive requests to the owning Mission Control task without connecting to or waking the sandbox. Serialize mutations and change local state only after success.
- Query both archived and non-archived tasks, retain archived sessions and their history, and reconcile task archive flags in both Agents and Editor windows, including connected environments.
- Preserve AHP behavior for additional sessions sharing the environment. Cancel stale account work and invalidate discovery responses started before a successful mutation.
- Add cross-client round-trip, offline restoration, request rejection, ordering, and shared remote-provider regression tests. Update the provider ownership documentation.

## Manual Verification

Live Mission Control mutation testing and UI end-to-end verification were not run; no live cloud sessions were modified. Archive endpoint paths and the task-list archive filter were checked against the existing Copilot API client and Mission Control OpenAPI contract.

To verify with two updated clients signed into the same account: archive a Cloud Sandbox session in one client, refresh discovery in the other, and confirm it is excluded from the non-archived list but available through the archive filter. Unarchive it and refresh the first client to confirm it returns. Repeat with a disconnected sandbox and an already-connected sandbox.

Updates propagate through the existing discovery refresh/polling path; this does not introduce a push channel.

(Written by Copilot)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The sequential awaits, refresh call path, 60-second stale trigger, and before/after request counts are all explicit in code and tests. Only the per-request duration varies by network conditions.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Every discovery now performs at least four sequential list requests instead of two; archived pagination adds up to 20 more sequential requests, and stale focused-window refreshes can repeat this once per minute.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased refresh and startup latency plus doubled steady-state discovery traffic
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Discovery iterated only the two repository scopes, so an empty or warm incremental refresh required two sequential list-task requests.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The changed scope list adds archived=true variants for both repository scopes, while the existing nested loop awaits every page and scope serially before discovery can reconcile sessions.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added archived scope entries at lines 298-299 expand the serial loop from `{withRepository:true/false}` to four `{withRepository, archived}` combinations; no parallelism or deferred archive path was added.
Findings.Title: Run archived discovery scopes concurrently with active scopes
Findings.Impact: Opening a window, manually refreshing sessions, or returning focus after the 60-second stale interval must wait for two additional network round trips even when the account has no archived tasks. Accounts with paginated archives can block reconciliation behind up to 20 additional list calls.
Findings.Evidence: `listSessions` awaits `_sendTask` inside nested scope/page loops, and `_doDiscoverAndSeed` awaits `listSessions` before publishing discovery. The updated tests explicitly raise warm incremental request count from 2 to 4 and a two-page scan from 3 to 5, proving the extra calls are on the critical path rather than background work.
Findings.Recommendation: Fetch the independent scope streams concurrently under a small shared limiter, preserving serial pagination and existing failure/checkpoint semantics within each stream, then merge their task maps before reconciliation.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The cold-cache condition, one-request-per-task mapping, concurrency limit, eager provider call path, and page bounds are explicit. The only uncertainty is how many archived tasks typical accounts have, which is reflected in medium severity.
Findings.PerformanceResource: per-task Mission Control detail GETs, provider objects, registrations, and persisted inventory entries
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On a cold process, each archived task is absent from `_discoveredTasks`, so all A archived summaries trigger A detail GETs in batches of five; the two archived scopes permit up to 2,000 distinct archived tasks before truncation.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: cold-start and full-refresh latency grows with the account's archived history
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Archived summaries were excluded by `!task.archived_at`, so normal startup discovery issued no detail GETs and created no environment providers for archived history.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: All cloud-sandbox summaries, including archived ones, now enter `sandboxTasks`; the existing `!cached?.session` branch fetches `/tasks/{id}` for each, and the caller eagerly seeds every returned session into a full per-environment provider.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Line 364 removes the prior `!task.archived_at` guard, newly feeding every archived task returned by the added archive scans into the existing per-task detail-expansion and provider-seeding path.
Findings.Title: Lazy-load archived task details instead of expanding the entire archive
Findings.Impact: A long-lived account with dozens or hundreds of archived sandboxes makes every fresh window process wait through many waves of detail requests before discovery completes, then retains a provider/controller and registrations per archived environment. At the supported 1,000-task-per-scope range this can dominate startup and memory.
Findings.Evidence: `sandboxTasks` feeds `Promise.all(sandboxTasks.map(... limiter.queue(...)))`; a cold cache always satisfies `!cached?.session`, causing one `_sendTask('/tasks/{id}')` per summary with concurrency 5. `_doDiscoverAndSeed` waits for that promise and calls `_seedDiscoveredSession` for every result, which invokes `_ensureProvider`. The test suite demonstrates discovery cardinality of 1,000 sessions for one scope.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep archived results as lightweight summaries and resolve their environment/session detail lazily or page-wise when archived rows are requested/opened; alternatively supply the binding in a batched list response. Do not eagerly send every archived task through the per-task detail/provider path during normal startup discovery.

Scenarios.Scenario: Window startup, manual session refresh, and stale-on-focus Cloud Sandbox discovery
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Authentication/account resolution, all task-list pages for every scope, all required task-detail and repository-name reads, session reconciliation/provider creation, and profile-inventory persistence complete before `_discoverAndSeed`/the refresh returns. None of the newly added archive discovery work is off the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List Mission Control tasks for active and archived repository scopes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Minimum 4 GETs per scan, up to 40 paginated GETs; before the diff the minimum was 2 and maximum 20.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only active with-repository and active without-repository scopes were queried.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All calls are awaited serially before reconciliation can start, directly increasing startup/manual refresh/focus-refresh latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch full Mission Control task detail for summaries lacking a cached session binding
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One GET per cold or changed task, concurrency 5. The diff newly adds up to 2,000 archived tasks to this population.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Archived tasks were filtered out and caused no detail GETs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery awaits all queued detail GETs before returning any reconciled result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve missing repository names through the GitHub REST API
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request per unique repository ID per process because promise results are cached; archived tasks can introduce additional unique IDs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only active discovered tasks could reach repository-name resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each affected task waits for repository resolution inside the detail limiter before discovery completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist minimal per-environment discovery inventory in profile storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One batched `storeAll` call per completed reconciliation, after O(N) serialization/comparison across all retained environments; only changed keys are written.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same boundary existed, but N contained active environments only; archived environments now increase its cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously after provider seeding and before `_doDiscoverAndSeed` returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Four task scopes (repository/no-repository × active/archived), up to 10 pages of 100 summaries per scope. Archived history therefore contributes up to 2,000 distinct summaries and, on a cold process, one detail expansion per archived task.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Discovery triggers are coalesced into one in-flight scan with at most one queued scan. Task-list scopes and pages are fully serialized. Task-detail GETs use a shared limiter of 5. Repository-name promises are cached/coalesced per repository ID.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Every scan still performs task-list requests. Incremental scans use a timestamp overlap, while full scans recur at least every 15 minutes. `_discoveredTasks` and repository-name caches suppress warm-process detail/name reads, but they are memory-only; persisted session inventory restores UI rows without warming the API cache, so a fresh process expands all archived summaries again.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: sequential awaits, cache conditions, concurrency limiter, refresh triggers, and before/after request counts are directly established by implementation and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network RTT and typical archived-task counts are not measured. The minimum request doubling, 30-second per-discovery-request timeout, cold-cache detail fan-out, page bounds, and provider cardinality are explicit, so uncertainty affects severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Scenarios.Verdict: Two reportable regressions: serialized archive scopes double the minimum discovery traffic/latency, and eager cold expansion creates O(archived history) detail requests and providers.

Scenarios.Scenario: User archives or unarchives an owning Cloud Sandbox session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The UI/provider sequencer awaits one Mission Control POST; only after success does it update local archive state and persist inventory. Sandbox connection/wake-up is explicitly not on this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one request per dequeued user mutation, with a 10-second timeout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Archive state changed locally with no network request, so it was not synchronized across clients.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local state and completion wait for the POST, preserving server-authoritative ordering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the changed environment inventory entry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One batched profile-storage update after each successful mutation, with unchanged entries skipped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Local provider state changed without updating the shared contribution inventory archive flag.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after the POST and before mutation completion; it does not wake or connect the sandbox.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One operation per user archive/unarchive action. Rapid toggles queue in order for that provider/controller.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A `Sequencer` serializes mutations per environment provider/controller. Independent environment controllers can operate concurrently, but a normal single-session toggle creates one request and no loop/burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful mutation deletes that task from `_discoveredTasks` and increments the discovery generation, preventing stale in-flight discovery from committing. There is no optimistic state cache; rejection retains the previous flag.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the single POST, sequencer, cancellation, cache invalidation, and post-success persistence are explicit and tested.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual POST latency varies, but cardinality and serialization are fixed and bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding. The added network boundary is the required cross-client mutation, is one-per-action, and is intentionally serialized without environment startup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cross-client archive reconciliation for disconnected or connected environments
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A normal discovery scan detects the archive timestamp change, fetches that task's detail if the cache summary differs, then updates the existing provider/controller archive observable and persists inventory. No AHP host action or sandbox connection is required.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Incremental active/archived task-list scan and changed-task detail read
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four minimum list GETs plus one detail GET for each changed archive timestamp; before the diff there were two list GETs and archived tasks were removed rather than retained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Discovery did not query archived scopes; an archived task was excluded/removed and no retained-session reconciliation occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All reads finish before another client's archive state becomes visible locally.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One batched storage call per completed discovery, writing only changed entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Inventory persistence existed, but had no Mission Control archive flag to reconcile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes as part of reconciliation; connected and disconnected environments use the same path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One changed task detail GET per remote archive transition on a warm cache; a cold scan scales with total archived history as covered in the startup scenario.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: List calls remain serial; changed detail reads share the concurrency-5 limiter. Local observable updates are synchronous and discovery itself is coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm summaries avoid unchanged task details; an `archived_at` difference forces the changed task detail read. Successful local mutations explicitly invalidate that task and stale discovery generation. Cold processes have no `_discoveredTasks` cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: timestamp comparison, detail-fetch condition, local update path, and absence of host connection are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cross-client update frequency is likely low; network latency is unmeasured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding beyond the discovery regressions already reported; a single changed-task detail read is bounded and necessary, while cold historical fan-out is covered by the second finding.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 13 changed files. Reported two diff-caused discovery regressions: serialized archive scopes double baseline task-list requests, and archived histories are eagerly expanded through per-task detail GETs and per-environment providers on cold discovery. Archive mutation sequencing and reconciliation are otherwise bounded and avoid sandbox wake-up.
